calendar.title: Ted's Dublin
calendar.byline: Curated by Ted · things I’d actually go to
calendar.description: Real Dublin this week: gigs, Georgian theatres, castle tours, seaside markets. Hand-picked, no filler.

events.title: Riverdance 30 – The New Generation
events.blurb: The 30th-anniversary edition of the Irish dance phenomenon runs all summer at its home theatre, with matinee and evening shows most days.

events.title: The Brightening Air by Conor McPherson
events.blurb: McPherson directs his own award-winning play about siblings in a 1980s rural Irish homestead, a Gate presentation of the Old Vic production.

events.title: Summer in Dublin – Free Weekend Street Events
events.blurb: Dublin City Council's free weekend series turns Parliament Street into a family playground with street performers, interactive shows and workshops.

events.title: Rembrandt to Matisse – A Celebration of European Prints and Drawings
events.blurb: Admission-free exhibition of around fifty of the Gallery's finest European works on paper, running 27 June to 8 November 2026.

events.title: Common Ground: Ireland and the EU
events.blurb: New multimedia exhibition timed to Ireland's EU presidency, exploring Irish influence in Europe, on show 1 July to 31 December 2026.

events.title: Making A Show of Myself
events.blurb: Moth Grand Slam champion Mary Kate O Flanagan performs six true stories in a solo show fresh from an off-Broadway run.

events.title: GAZE International LGBTQIA Film Festival
events.blurb: Ireland's long-running queer film festival, founded in 1992, screens features and shorts across two city cinemas.

events.title: A New Form of Beauty: Dublin Youth Culture, Street Style and Subculture 1960s-1990s
events.blurb: Photographic exhibition of Dublin street style and subcultures from the 1960s to 1990s, in its final month at Collins Barracks.
events.venue: National Museum of Ireland – Decorative Arts & History, Collins Barracks

events.title: Historical Walking Tours of Dublin (The Original Tour)
events.blurb: Two-hour tour led by history professionals covering the English conquest through the peace process, running daily in season since 1986.

events.title: Dublin Literary Pub Crawl
events.blurb: Actor-led nightly summer walk through four historic pubs and Trinity College, performing Joyce, Beckett, Wilde and Behan along the way.
events.venue: The Duke Pub, 9 Duke Street (start point)

events.title: Fawlty Towers – The Play
events.blurb: John Cleese's stage adaptation of the classic sitcom plays a five-night Dublin run after a sold-out West End season.
